prompt.context: Your client is a diversified industrials distributor that focuses on four key product areas: plumbing tools (pipes, installation tools), lumber residential products (siding, framing materials, roofing), cement (raw cement powder, ready-to-use cement, mixing tools, etc.) and paper products (cardboard, writing paper, packaging paper, etc.). The client distributes finished products to a variety of customers, such as property management companies, residential home builders and contractor plumbers. Your client currently faces an issue of bottom-line growth. We have been engaged to study how our client can increase their EBITDA margin over the next 5 years.
prompt.question: How can our client increase their EBITDA margin over the next 5 years?

clarifying_info.q: Does the client operate internationally or have plans to expand internationally?
clarifying_info.a: The client operates only in the USA and does not want to expand internationally.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's current market position?
clarifying_info.a: The client has many competitors and operates in a fragmented industry, owning only 10% of market share.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's current strategy?
clarifying_info.a: The current strategy is to acquire smaller, competing distributors that have a good synergistic fit.

clarifying_info.q: Does the client manufacture any products?
clarifying_info.a: No. The client does not manufacture but serves as an intermediary — a distributor — to distribute products to end-customers.

clarifying_info.q: What are the client's current financials?
clarifying_info.a: The client achieved revenues of $15B and an EBITDA margin of 8% in 2020.

clarifying_info.q: What is the EBITDA margin target?
clarifying_info.a: The target is an EBITDA margin of 10% on whatever revenue by 2025.

exhibits.title: Projected market growth of entire construction materials space (USA-only, %)
exhibits.shows: A side-by-side composition chart showing the percentage breakdown of the construction materials market in 2020 and 2025 by product category.

exhibits.title: Paper-based products EBITDA margins (USA-only, 2020-2025)
exhibits.shows: A scatter plot with EBITDA margin (%) on the x-axis (ranging roughly 5-18%) and CAGR for the next 5 years (%) on the y-axis (ranging roughly 0.5-7%), with bubble size representing market size. Six paper sub-categories are plotted: Commercial writing paper, Large-box packaging, Bathroom hygiene wipes, Small-box packaging, Paper towels, and Specialized paper products.

framework: Core product expansion: conduct market analysis (current markets served, competitor scan, CAGR) for each of the four product categories to identify where growth is highest
Value-added services: offer installation services, provide a digital tool for on-demand ordering and tracking, rent out tools/equipment
New product categories: expand into adjacent categories such as decking/fencing materials, flooring, or other construction materials
Backward integration: acquire a manufacturer in one of the product categories (e.g., a plumbing supplies manufacturer or paper pulp facility)
Risk assessment: evaluate supplier risks, channel conflict, volatility, management/human capital fit, and external factors such as recession or construction downturns

questions.prompt: Walk me through Exhibit 1. What does it tell you, and what should the client prioritize?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note the axes are in reverse order between 2020 and 2025. Candidate should calculate the 5-year % change in market share for each product category and prioritize the highest positive-change categories. Strong candidates note the change direction and rank by magnitude: paper (+33%), plumbing (+25%), other (-25%), lumber (-33%). Candidate should recommend deep-diving into paper-based products and plumbing next. Second-order insight: ask what EBITDA margins look like for these growing categories.

math.setup: Calculate % change in market composition share for each category from 2020 to 2025
math.answer: Paper-based products and plumbing tools show the strongest projected 5-year growth; lumber should be avoided.

questions.prompt: Now look at Exhibit 2. Which paper sub-category should the client focus on, and why?
questions.guidance: No math required. Basic insight: Commercial writing paper has the greatest EBITDA margin; Specialized paper products have the greatest CAGR; Bathroom hygiene wipes should be avoided due to low CAGR. Second-order insight: depends on client's risk appetite — commercial writing paper satisfies the primary goal of improving EBITDA margin; small-box packaging presents an opportunity depending on market fragmentation. Candidate should ask about market size and key players to assess whether acquisition of smaller players is feasible.

brainstorming.prompt: What should the client consider while expanding into the paper products space? Specifically, what are some possible advantages and disadvantages of this expansion strategy?

categories.name: Opportunities
ideas: Paper products industry, specifically commercial writing products, can help expand into the commercial space (restaurants, bars, clubs, office spaces)
Capacity to expand abroad since paper products are global
Can acquire a local paper mill to both manufacture and distribute, capturing more margin

categories.name: Challenges / Risks
ideas: Lack of management expertise in new geographies or sub-categories (e.g., how business is conducted in global markets vs. the current US market)
Channel conflict with existing customers or suppliers if entering manufacturing
Volatility and cyclicality in paper demand (e.g., shift to digital reducing commercial writing paper demand over time)
Human capital and integration risk from acquisitions

recommendation: Continue to focus on core products and specifically expand within the paper products space, targeting a 10% overall EBITDA margin trajectory over the coming 5 years
Additional levers: pursue operational excellence to reduce operational costs, and stay close to core products rather than expanding into entirely new verticals
risks: Supplier risks if backward integration is pursued
Channel conflict from potential manufacturing acquisitions
External macro factors: recession, construction downturn, raw materials access
Management and human capital risk from M&A integration
next_steps: Identify which paper-based sub-product category (e.g., commercial writing paper) is most impactful to improve EBITDA by assessing key players and market fragmentation
Evaluate potential acquisition targets in the paper products space to grow market share and achieve the 10% EBITDA margin target by 2025
